system_architecture.description: CSF shunt catheter with S. aureus phage K immobilized on electrospun titanium-coated surface; phages prevent biofilm formation by infecting and lysing S. aureus before biofilm establishes

subsystems.name: Catheter body (substrate)
subsystems.function: Carries CSF flow + supports electrospun Ti coating

subsystems.name: Electrospun titanium coating
subsystems.function: High-surface-area substrate for phage immobilization; Ti has known antibacterial properties
subsystems.evidence_source: R332 mechanism + external Ti coating literature

subsystems.name: Phage K immobilization layer
subsystems.function: S. aureus phage K bound to Ti surface; infects and lyses S. aureus on contact
subsystems.evidence_source: R332 mechanism + external phage K literature (PMC6693497)

subsystems.name: Stabilization matrix for phage viability
subsystems.function: Preserves phage infectivity over implantation lifetime (likely trehalose or lyoprotectant)

key_equations: mu = mu_max * S / (Ks + S) [Monod specific growth rate]
microbiological_model.phage_bacteria_kinetics: Phage adsorbs to S. aureus cell surface at rate k_ads * [Phage] * [Bacteria]; infection leads to lysis and release of new phages
microbiological_model.biofilm_prevention_target: Prevent biofilm establishment in first 24-48h (critical window for shunt infection)
microbiological_model.critical_parameter: Phage surface density Gamma_phage (PFU/cm^2); must exceed threshold for prophylactic lysis

safety_invariants.INV-1: Phage K specifically infects S. aureus (host range specificity)
safety_invariants.INV-2: Phage remains viable over target implantation lifetime
safety_invariants.INV-3: No phage-mediated adverse effects on host tissue

mechanism_architecture.physical_changes: S. aureus cells contacting phage-coated surface adsorb phages, become infected, and lyse before establishing biofilm
mechanism_architecture.key_physics: Phage adsorption kinetics: dP/dt = -k_ads * [Phage_surface] * [Bacteria]. At sufficient phage surface density, bacterial colonization rate < lysis rate, preventing biofilm establishment.

kinetic_model.model: Surface colonization: dN_bact/dt = k_attach * [Bact] - k_lysis * [Phage] * [Bact_surface]; net growth or decay depends on phage density
kinetic_model.prediction_horizon: 48-72h prophylactic window (critical for shunt infection prevention)
kinetic_model.status: MODELLED — based on published phage kinetics; no in vitro verification on this coating

design_inputs.value: Infection = 8-12% of shunt failures, $40-80K per case. Antibiotic resistance emerging (R332)
S. aureus phage K immobilized on electrospun Ti-coated catheter surface; prevents biofilm formation
Staphylococcus aureus (primary shunt pathogen, per literature)
Log reduction >= 3 (99.9%) at 24h vs S. aureus (ASTM E2180)

governing_model.summary: Phage-bacteria adsorption kinetics on immobilized phage surface. Surface phage density must exceed threshold such that bacterial lysis rate exceeds colonization rate during the critical 24-48h post-implantation window.
equations: mu = mu_max * S / (Ks + S) [Monod specific growth rate]
Gamma_phage(t) = Gamma_0 * exp(-k_decay * t) [phage surface density decay]
Threshold: k_lysis * Gamma_phage(t) > k_attach * [Bact]_challenge for t in [0, t_critical]
assumptions: Phage K host range limited to S. aureus (literature-supported)
